_meta.purpose: Curriculum-design learnings mined from our own cohort data. Both Mastery proposals (Expert & Authority, AI for Founders) read from this file so the same mistake is never designed in twice.

sources.SIM: appKlfvxdXofNlFfk — Speaking & Influence Mastery: 84 lesson records across 2025 (492 enrolled) and 2026 (456 enrolled), plus 148 detractor feedback submissions (rating ≤6)
sources.AIM: appHS19yXObg8sHZv — AI Summit & Mastery: 176 lesson records, 2023–2026 cohorts

data_hygiene: AIM records from 2023–24 cohorts use a 5-POINT scale (e.g. 'Build Applications with Glide' 5.00/5 = perfect, not 5/10). Never rank across cohorts without checking the scale. The 'bottom of base' is mostly scale confusion, not bad sessions.
SIM 2025 per-lesson ratings live in the comparison rollup, not the base's Avg Rating lookup — the base carries 2025 attendance only.
Single-vote rows (n=1–3) appear throughout every base and must be excluded before any ranking.

learnings.name: A multi-day intensive on the mainline cadence breaks retention permanently
learnings.evidence: SIM 2025: show-up averaged ~57% across sessions 1–9. The One Talk Workshop ran as three consecutive mainline sessions: 39% → 31% → 34%. Attendance NEVER recovered — the post-OTW half of the programme ran 45% declining to 33%, a permanent ~14-point break in the curve.
learnings.rule: A multi-day intensive must not consume mainline slots. Run it as an optional weekend block; the Tue/Thu cadence continues uninterrupted around it.
learnings.verified_fix: SIM 2026 ran the same 3-day OTW as an unrated weekend Bonus (Fri–Sun, Aug 7–9). The next mainline sessions held at 56% and 58%. The fix is proven, not theoretical.

learnings.name: Off-cadence add-on sessions die regardless of teacher quality
learnings.evidence: SIM 2025: Paul McKenna — the base's strongest guest asset (9.61–9.62) — drew 23% (112/492) for an off-rhythm Monday add-on, the worst attendance in the base. Dr. Shadé Zahrai's off-cadence session: 26%.
learnings.rule: Never schedule content outside the established weekly rhythm. If it matters, it gets a mainline slot; if it doesn't fit, it becomes a recorded bonus.

learnings.name: Teacher substitution destroys a session
learnings.evidence: SIM 2025: the Strategic Storytelling workshop swapped Eric Edmeades for a substitute host. It drew 24 detractor submissions — the most of any session in the base. Verbatim: 'Not organized, changed speaker, very disjointed, disappointed.'
learnings.rule: Announce the named teacher only when confirmed, and never swap after announcement. A cancelled session damages less than a substituted one.

learnings.name: Breakout rooms are the #1 detractor theme
learnings.evidence: 20 of 148 SIM detractor comments mention breakout rooms — the largest single theme, ahead of tech issues (7) and length (5).
learnings.rule: Breakouts only with a tight artefact-producing brief, a time-box, and an opt-out. Never as filler.

learnings.name: A long single-lead programme hits a repetition cliff around month two
learnings.evidence: SIM 2025 ran ~46 sessions with one lead teacher. Verbatim detractor: 'Lost interest since 2nd month… it's been pretty much the same topic. Now it feels more like a chit chat session than a real Mastery.'
learnings.rule: Rotate named authors on the teach slot and make each week ship a distinct artefact, so no two weeks feel interchangeable. 17–18 weeks, not 20+.

learnings.name: Q&A-only and low-content sessions are punished
learnings.evidence: SIM 2025 detractors: 'I was disappointed that this was only Q&A — would have loved more content' (Professional Speaking week). AIM unstructured community calls: 5.89.
learnings.rule: Every live touchpoint has a job and a deliverable. Q&A attaches to content; it is never the content.

learnings.name: Scope drift into a neighbouring programme's territory generates refund requests
learnings.evidence: SIM 2025 detractor on the product-creation week: 'I'm only interested in speaking, not creating a course or teaching or creating a business.' Another student asked about refund timing when early weeks felt like business prep. SIM's back half (Getting Booked, Business Models for Speakers, Productizing Your Message) is Expert & Authority territory taught to a speaking audience.
learnings.rule: Each programme teaches its own promise and cross-refers for the rest. The three-programme boundary (SIM = the talk, E&A = the business of being known, AIF = the machine) is a retention mechanism, not just marketing.

learnings.name: Abstract kickoffs fail; kickoffs are structurally weak even when competent
learnings.evidence: AIM 'Kick Off & Define Your Vision in the Age of AI' (Mindvalley Team): 6.04, n=116, in front of 661. Even Vishen's own 2025 AIM kickoff only hit 8.47. Kickoff type average across AIM: 7.26 — the weakest session type.
learnings.rule: Open with a build that produces a personal win in session one. Keep the kickoff short on vision and long on doing.

learnings.name: The paired Teach → Workshop cadence holds a room — but the workshop needs its own owner
learnings.evidence: SIM 2026 (paired cadence): last-3-session attendance 56.4% vs 41.5% in 2025. But SIM 2026 workshops rate 9.25 vs 9.55 for lessons — every workshop below every teach bar the opener. AIM's dedicated-owner labs average 9.2 with a 9.46 ceiling.
learnings.rule: Keep the paired cadence. Give the workshop slot a named owner whose only job is implementation, and require a shipped artefact per session.

learnings.name: Capstone integration sessions are the highest-rated thing we run
learnings.evidence: AIM 'Tying Everything Together' (Vykintas): 9.87 n=99 — the top-rated session in the base, plus 9.66 for its Q&A and 9.46 for its lab. SIM 2026's highest is also an integrative session (Story, 9.74).
learnings.rule: Design an explicit integration moment where students assemble everything into one working thing. Do not leave integration implicit.

learnings.name: Claims drift when documents cite documents
learnings.evidence: The AI Founders proposal cites 'a perfect-10 Implementation Lab'. The base shows labs from 8.14 to 9.46 — no 10 exists (the 9.87 was the capstone teach). The author deck's 'Chris Do 9.83, highest in SMM' is 9.78 and ranks 6th. Natalie Ellis 9.25 is 9.16.
learnings.rule: Every figure in a proposal is re-derived from the base and carries its sample size. data/authors.json is the only citation source.

learnings.finding: The Critic Path: become the niche's trusted reviewer before its teacher. Remote-viewing blog: 70% opt-in on a coming-soon pop-up, biggest list in the niche in 6 months, $970K in 18 months via 50% revenue-share webinars.
learnings.status: Vishen's own account, not independently verified

learnings.finding: Three Founder Stories: vision ('imagine a world where…', 10 years ahead, mission not product), plan (backward staircase yr 1/3/6/10, what+why never how), values (wound→fury→change ×3 → manifesto). Partner-scoring exercise: describe, score 1-10, rewrite, rescore.
learnings.status: framework from stage; Nora Cavani Forbes story as proof point
learnings.applied_to: E&A W4 teach+lab, W8 story bank

learnings.finding: AOV mechanics: order bumps ($9-17 zero-cost tools), upsell 1, downsell, upsell 2; price-test 29/39/49; webinar needed above ~$500, under $99 sells off a single ad/reel; commenters ~3x more likely to buy.

30-day rule: days 1-7 over-deliver + drive consumption; days 8-14 engagement, no selling; days 14-28 free monthly summit sells high ticket; solopreneur recoups ad spend in 30 days (Mindvalley as publisher: 9 months).

Change is a witness problem, not a willpower problem (expectancy effect). Identity sabbatical exercise; accountability by witnessing (Friday text; commitments kept for others per Gretchen Rubin); 'masters never change their mind'.
learnings.applied_to: E&A W1 + Show Up track doctrine

learnings.source: MVU 2026 stage talk Day 2 — Mentimeter, 196 respondents
learnings.finding: Imposter syndrome was the #2 most-voted audience question on becoming an expert/authority.
Faceless Instagram posts (B-roll + caption) earning $40-50K/month via ManyChat comment-to-DM into the S&I webinar funnel selling a $5K programme.
learnings.status: Vishen's own account of his funnel

learnings.finding: 2022 ad test: 42 ads produced, 4 worked (~10%); those four pulled ~quarter-billion dollars over three years. Doctrine: the most important skill is operational efficiency in testing.
Daniel Priestley's 8-hour MVU accelerator scored NPS 90 — 'higher NPS than the iPhone when it was first released'.
learnings.status: stated from stage; corroborates the separately reported 84-NPS AIM lab data

learnings.finding: Masterclass sales total: 'half a billion' on the accelerator stage vs 'between 400 million to half a billion' on the Day 2 stage. Carry the range $400-500M; both are self-reported.
learnings.applied_to: both proposals — range used, legal flag refreshed

learnings.finding: Build cost for software down 97% since February 2026 ($100K → $3K); build speed up ~50x. Basis of the 'why now' for founder-built products.

Portfolio positioning system adopted: one-verb promises (E&A 'Be chosen.', AIF 'Run on AI.'), signature diagnostic sentences ('I'm great at what I do, but nobody knows me.' / 'My business can't run a single day without me.'), and neighbour boundary lines (Speaking vs Authority: room asks for you; Social vs Authority: chosen by the right ones; AI Mastery vs AIF: transforms you vs your business).

three_programme_boundary.speaking_influence: The talk. Stagecraft, story delivery, confidence, holding a room. Ends where monetisation begins.
three_programme_boundary.expert_authority: The business of being known. Niche, product ladder, masterclass, traffic, the close. Assumes you can speak; teaches you how to be found and paid.
three_programme_boundary.ai_founders: The machine. Five pillars rebuilt as AI systems for someone who already has something to sell. Assumes demand exists; teaches you how to serve it without drowning.
three_programme_boundary.router: Can't hold a room → SIM. Can hold a room but nobody's buying → E&A. People are buying and it's eating you alive → AIF.
three_programme_boundary.evidence: SIM detractors explicitly rejected business-building content inside a speaking programme (L7). The boundary is what students are telling us they want.
